2009.note: A warm, generous year of ripe, rounded wines with soft acidity. Mature now; drink rather than keep. Its drinking window runs roughly from 2013 to 2032.

2008.note: A cool, classic year of high-acid, long-lived Riesling and fine VT. Mature and splendid now. Its drinking window runs roughly from 2012 to 2038.

2007.note: An early spring and a long autumn produced fine dry wines and excellent late-harvest wines. Mature now; the VT and SGN will keep longer.

2006.note: Rain and rot at harvest made a difficult year with dilute or botrytis-marked wines. Past its best now. Its drinking window closed around 2020; treat any survivor as a curiosity.

2005.note: A balanced, ripe year of very good wines with good acidity. Mature now and best drunk over the next few years.

2004.note: A cool, large crop of classic, fresh wines. Mature now; drink up the grand crus while they are still lively.

2003.note: The heatwave made heavy, low-acid, sometimes bitter wines untypical of Alsace. Past its best now. Its drinking window closed around 2018; treat any survivor as a curiosity.

2002.note: A classic year of balanced, fresh wines with good Riesling. Mature now; drink up. The window closes around 2028, so open remaining bottles soon.

2001.note: A fine year with good dry Riesling and late-harvest wines. Mature now; drink up the dry wines. The window closes around 2028, so open remaining bottles soon.

2000.note: A ripe but uneven year with some rot, better for Pinot Gris than Riesling. Past its best now. Its drinking window closed around 2022; treat any survivor as a curiosity.

1999.note: A large crop of soft, early-maturing wines with modest acidity. Past its best now. Its drinking window closed around 2020; treat any survivor as a curiosity.

1998.note: A year with fine VT and SGN after a botrytis-rich autumn; dry wines were more modest. Past their best for dry wines.

1997.note: A ripe, balanced year from a warm, dry autumn. Past its best for most dry wines; sweet wines survive. Its drinking window closed around 2025; treat any survivor as a curiosity.

1996.note: A cool year of high-acid, long-lived Riesling that took years to open. Drink up now. The window closes around 2028, so open remaining bottles soon.

1995.note: A year of botrytis and fine sweet wines; dry wines were uneven. Past their best for dry wines. Its drinking window closed around 2025; treat any survivor as a curiosity.

1994.note: An uneven, rain-affected year with some good late-harvest wines. Past its best now. Its drinking window closed around 2018; treat any survivor as a curiosity.

1993.note: A good, classic year of fresh, balanced wines. Past its best now. Its drinking window closed around 2015; treat any survivor as a curiosity.

1992.note: A large, soft crop of easy-drinking wines without much structure. Past its best now. Its drinking window closed around 2012; treat any survivor as a curiosity.

1991.note: A light, cool year with lean wines and few late-harvest bottlings. Past its best now. Its drinking window closed around 2008; treat any survivor as a curiosity.

1990.note: A great year of rich, concentrated wines, including legendary SGN from the leading houses. Mature now; dry grand crus should be drunk.

1989.note: A great year for VT and SGN after a warm, botrytis-rich autumn. Mature now; the sweet wines will keep for years.

1983.note: A great, rich vintage with fine dry Riesling and superb late-harvest wines. Mature now; the best sweet wines survive. The window closes around 2030, so open remaining bottles soon.

1976.note: A legendary year for SGN after a hot drought summer, with Hugel's wines among the most famous. Mature now and still remarkable.

1971.note: A great vintage of balance and acidity, with long-lived Riesling. Mature now; only well-stored bottles remain worth opening. Its drinking window closed around 2025; treat any survivor as a curiosity.

2024.note: A cool, wet year with mildew and hail in several crus cut yields. Light, fresh, low-alcohol Gamay with charm; drink the crus young and pick producers who sorted carefully.

2023.note: A large crop ripened in late-summer heat, with hail in places. Ripe, supple, juicy crus; the best Morgon and Moulin-à-Vent have depth for a decade.

2022.note: Drought and heat gave a small crop of rich, ripe, concentrated Gamay. Very good; top crus are open and will keep.

2021.note: Frost and a cool summer made fresh, light, classic Beaujolais with bright acidity and modest alcohol, close to the old style. Drinking now.

2020.note: A hot, early year of concentrated, ripe, structured crus with real tannin. Excellent; top Morgon and Moulin-à-Vent are at an early peak.

2019.note: Hail, frost and heat cut yields, giving concentrated, structured crus with good freshness. Very good and at their peak now.

2018.note: A sunny, generous year of ripe, plush, excellent Gamay across all ten crus. At its peak now; the best Moulin-à-Vent will hold.

2017.note: Hail struck Fleurie and its neighbours, but the crop elsewhere was good, balanced and juicy. Mature now; drink over the next few years.

2016.note: Hail and frost hit several crus; the rest made fresh, balanced wines of medium weight. Mature now; drink up. Its drinking window runs roughly from 2019 to 2028.

2015.note: A hot, dry year of great, rich, concentrated crus, Moulin-à-Vent especially. Mature and holding at the top. Its drinking window runs roughly from 2018 to 2032.

2014.note: A fine September rescued the year, giving fresh, classic crus with lovely fruit and good acidity. Mature now; drink up.

2013.note: A cold spring and a late harvest gave fresh, light crus with high acidity. Past its best now. Its drinking window closed around 2024; treat any survivor as a curiosity.

2012.note: Hail and rot made a tiny, difficult vintage with lean wines. Past its best now. Its drinking window closed around 2022; treat any survivor as a curiosity.

2011.note: An early, warm year of ripe, generous crus. Drink up now; only top Moulin-à-Vent still has much to give. The window closes around 2026, so open remaining bottles soon.

2010.note: A small crop of concentrated, structured crus with good acidity. Drink up now; Morgon Côte du Py has held best.

2009.note: A hot, celebrated year of rich, ripe, concentrated crus that sold out quickly. Drink up the remaining bottles. Its drinking window runs roughly from 2012 to 2030.

2008.note: A wet year of light, sometimes dilute Gamay with little to keep it going. Past its best now. Its drinking window closed around 2016; treat any survivor as a curiosity.

2007.note: A wet summer gave light, early-drinking wines with modest fruit. Past its best now. Its drinking window closed around 2015; treat any survivor as a curiosity.

2006.note: A good, balanced year of fresh crus for medium-term drinking. Past its best now. Its drinking window closed around 2018; treat any survivor as a curiosity.

2005.note: A great, structured vintage for the crus, especially Moulin-à-Vent and Morgon. Drink up now from good cellars. The window closes around 2028, so open remaining bottles soon.

2004.note: A light, rainy year of thin Gamay without much ageing potential. Past its best for every cru. Its drinking window closed around 2012; treat any survivor as a curiosity.

2003.note: The heatwave made rich, alcoholic, sometimes jammy crus that impressed in youth. Past its best now. Its drinking window closed around 2022; treat any survivor as a curiosity.

2002.note: A wet harvest and rot made a poor vintage across the region. Past its best now. Its drinking window closed around 2010; treat any survivor as a curiosity.

2001.note: A wet year of light, lean wines that were best within a few years. Past its best now. Its drinking window closed around 2010; treat any survivor as a curiosity.

2000.note: A good year of supple, fruity crus for early and medium-term drinking. Past its best now. Its drinking window closed around 2012; treat any survivor as a curiosity.

1999.note: A good year of ripe, balanced crus with good structure in Moulin-à-Vent. Past its best now. Its drinking window closed around 2012; treat any survivor as a curiosity.

1998.note: A good year of fresh, balanced crus for medium-term drinking. Past its best now. Its drinking window closed around 2010; treat any survivor as a curiosity.

1997.note: A ripe, warm year of soft, generous crus that drank early. Past its best now. Its drinking window closed around 2010; treat any survivor as a curiosity.

1996.note: A fresh, high-acid year of lighter crus that aged reasonably. Past its best now. Its drinking window closed around 2008; treat any survivor as a curiosity.

1995.note: A good year of ripe, attractive crus for medium-term drinking. Past its best now. Its drinking window closed around 2008; treat any survivor as a curiosity.

1994.note: A wet year of light, dilute Gamay with little to offer now. Past its best now. Its drinking window closed around 2004; treat any survivor as a curiosity.

1993.note: A wet year of lean crus with little ageing potential. Past its best now. Its drinking window closed around 2004; treat any survivor as a curiosity.

1992.note: A light, large crop of easy, short-lived Gamay. Past its best now. Its drinking window closed around 2002; treat any survivor as a curiosity.

1991.note: A very good year for the crus, ripe and structured, long underrated. Past its best now. Its drinking window closed around 2008; treat any survivor as a curiosity.

1990.note: A ripe, warm year of rich, generous crus with real depth. Past its best now. Its drinking window closed around 2008; treat any survivor as a curiosity.

2024.note: A wet spring, hail and mildew, then a generous crop that struggled to build sugar. Expect lighter, lower-alcohol Barolo with bright acidity; selection decided quality. Released from 2028.

2023.note: Spring rain and disease pressure, hail in places and an August heatwave brought an early harvest. Barbaresco from the year is mid-weight with polished tannins; Barolo, released in 2027, looks similar and uneven.

2022.note: A dry winter and a hot, dry summer cut yields by 30 to 40 percent. Open aromatics and fine-grained tannins at best, dilution and alcohol over 15 percent at worst. Serralunga was most consistent; earlier drinking than 2021.

2021.note: A long, even season with cool nights produced classic, perfumed, deeply structured Barolo with bright acidity, widely hailed as exceptional. Built for decades; leave the crus alone.

2020.note: A warm year without extremes gave elegant, aromatic, supple Barolo with ripe tannins and early charm. Very good; the classic bottlings are nearly ready.

2019.note: A cool spring, a warm summer and a long autumn produced fresh, structured, classically proportioned Barolo with high acidity. A great vintage still in its youth.

2018.note: A wet spring and a humid summer brought disease and uneven ripening. Lighter, perfumed, early-drinking Barolo; the best are charming and graceful. Drinking now.

2017.note: Spring frost, then extreme heat and drought. Ripe fruit with firm, sometimes drying tannins; quality is uneven, best in cooler, higher sites. Approachable now.
